A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDTT research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and unchanged generated-text examples.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation, LAMBADA, distillation-ablation, model-scaling and latency results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds multiple-choice benchmark results, diversity measurements, numerical-precision experiments and additional latency evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, teacher-target construction, model architecture and KLD/TVD/log-space MSE objectives remain unchanged. Iterative student-to-teacher distillation already appears in v1 Section 4.1; v2 explains it more explicitly in Section 3. The added chi-squared discussion does not introduce an implemented training loss.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, MathQA, PIQA and WinoGrande (Table 1), substantially extending downstream coverage beyond LAMBADA to multiple-choice tasks. OpenWebText training and WebText generation evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The scaling LAMBADA comparison changes from AR small/medium/large references in v1 Figure 15 to Teacher, GPT-2 small and Re-trained AR in v2 Figure 17. V2 also includes ordinary and nucleus-sampled GPT-2 references in conditional-perplexity/diversity comparisons. The new multiple-choice benchmarks otherwise reuse existing comparator families.

E3.justification: V2 adds float64 sampling and backward-KL computation, self-BLEU, continuation-only perplexity and multiple-choice accuracy evaluation. Latency testing expands from the original 1.3B, batch-size-8 experiment to six sizes spanning 169M–8B and batch sizes 4 and 8. The original core training schedule remains.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to numerical precision, diversity versus generation quality, and latency across model sizes and batch sizes. V2 also reports that continuously increasing the sampling step size within one model caused divergence after 30–50 steps. Existing round-length, sampler and optimizer/EMA ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten latency measurements after one warm-up. V2 introduces no new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure; the additional figures and table retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for the new benchmarks and analyses. Table 1 reports teacher/KLD-student accuracies of 40.91/40.57 on ARC-Easy and 59.74/59.85 on PIQA. New figures report conditional perplexity, diversity, float64 outcomes and expanded latency measurements. The main LAMBADA plot also swaps the Teacher and GPT-2 small reference-line labels between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds the chi-squared divergence definition, its weighted squared-error identity and its distinction from log-space MSE. Existing diffusion and distillation mathematics remain; Equation 7 primarily formalizes the already-used iterative procedure, without a new proof.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly extends contribution claims to conditional generation and preservation of performance across six additional multiple-choice benchmarks. It qualifies the headline 8× speedup with the 1.3B scale and 16 decoding steps. The central SDTT acceleration and scalability claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains why deterministic decoding from an entirely masked initialization would produce only one sample, warns that low-precision sampling can distort perplexity and diversity, and interprets self-BLEU results as limited diversity loss compared with AR distillation. These add substantive explanations and qualifications to the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses FlashAttention, bfloat16 sampling and architecture configurations for 1.3B/3B/8B models. It drops v1's explicit unconditional-generation sample-count description. Section 7 also removes the GitHub/HuggingFace access links and replaces the stated code/checkpoint release with a future release upon de-anonymization; this changes documented access, without establishing actual online availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and brief positioning around numerical-precision artifacts, diversity, DiMS, reparameterized discrete diffusion and Diffusion of Thoughts. Most related-work discussion and the central distinction from continuous-diffusion distillation remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introduction and iterative-SDTT explanation, reorganizes evaluation descriptions, retitles Section 4.1, removes the TL;DR box and adds acknowledgements and conference headers. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds a first-page perplexity–latency plot, downstream-results table and precision, diversity and latency displays. It expands the architecture table, redistributes main-text panels and moves the original latency comparison into an appendix grid. Numerous retained plots receive revised axes, round labels, legends and captions.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked explicit checks for diversity loss and sampling-precision artifacts behind its perplexity results. V2's self-BLEU and float64 experiments address these important validation gaps, while broader downstream evaluation and direct perplexity–latency comparisons strengthen the central speed–quality argument. Removing code/checkpoint links and size-matched AR references from the scaling plot are setbacks, but the stronger validation provides a substantial net quality improvement.
